transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, I'm here because I've been really bothered by this scar on my wrist lately. I mean, I know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me, but... I just can't seem to stop focusing on it. When I’m at church, or sitting around the table playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it. It just feels like it’s the very first thing they notice about me now.
Do you believe your wrist scar looks noticeably unattractive or abnormal to other people?

Yes, I do. Like I was just saying, deep down I know it's probably not as bad as my mind makes it out to be. But... yes, I think it looks very unattractive and abnormal. That's exactly why I feel like everyone's eyes go straight to it when I'm at church or sitting at the bridge table. Even if I try to tell myself otherwise, I just assume they see this ugly mark and it's the only thing they're looking at.
Because of the scar, do you find yourself repeatedly checking it or trying to hide it?

Yes, I do. Before I leave the house, I usually stop at the hall mirror and check my wrist a few times. I definitely try to hide it... I'll test out different sleeves, or put on a wide bracelet to see if that covers it up. And sometimes I'll ask my husband if it looks obvious before we go anywhere. He always tells me it’s barely there, but I still feel the need to check.
Because of your wrist scar, do you avoid going to church, bridge, or other social situations?

Yes, I do sometimes. I try not to let it stop me entirely, but... I have skipped some of my choir and theater volunteer commitments lately. I just get so caught up at the house trying to make sure my wrist won't be noticed, and sometimes it just feels easier to stay home. 

It’s actually affecting my job a bit, too. I do bookkeeping from home, and... well, I’ve been late turning in some of my work recently because I'm just so distracted by all of this.
If your wrist scar were completely gone, would you still feel very anxious in social situations like church or bridge?

No, I really don't think so. Um, the anxiety is pretty much just about the scar. If it were completely gone... well, I'm sure I'd feel fine. I've always enjoyed going to church and playing bridge, and I never used to get nervous about being around people before I started worrying so much about my wrist.
